notes:
Topline: evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for regulated payments workload. Primary ask: hard latency SLOs, throughput guarantees, and an enterprise SLA with explicit credit schedule and maintenance rules.

Key SLA asks (customer):
- Uptime: 99.99% target for production region (wants 99.995 on core payment flows).
- Credits: tiered credit schedule requested: 5% credit if monthly uptime <99.99 but >=99.95; 15% if <99.95 but >=99.9; 30% if <99.9. Customer pushing for quicker credit process (auto-apply vs manual claim).
- Maintenance windows: prefer 02:00-05:00 UTC monthly, max 3 hours, 72h advance notice for planned maint; major upgrades require 30 days notice and optional opt-out for high-risk windows.
- Support SLAs: P1 (production-down): 30 min ack, 2 hr mitigation update, 24x7 escalation path; P2: 2 hr ack, 8 hr update; P3: next business day. Named on-call + escalation matrix required in SOW.

Throughput / capacity planning notes:
- Baseline workload: chat-based customer support + embeddings for fraud signals. Expected peak: 150 concurrent chat sessions, 10k embeddings/day, 200 rps for simple reranking endpoints during batch jobs.
- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 120ms for short chat responses (≤128 tokens), p95 <= 450ms. Reranking p95 <= 600ms (batch-aware).
- Reserved GPU ask: initial commit = 8 x A100-equivalent workers (aiming to sustain 150 concurrent chat RPS with 50ms batching window). Customer asked for explicit burst capacity policy (extra nodes available within 20 minutes with pre-negotiated rate).
- Cache and warmup: want guaranteed prefix cache hit guidance and pre-warmed KV caches as part of Dedicated onboarding.

Procurement/legal highlights:
- Legal flagged indemnity and data residency clauses. Need SOC2 Type II artifacts (controls narrative + last report). Compliance team requested KMS/HSM architecture diagram.
- Finance: wants monthly invoicing with true-up, and a 12-month committed term with quarterly usage reconciliation.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We need a playbook for when latency spikes — who calls who, and how credits are triggered." — Head of Ops
- "If you can commit to 99.99% with auto credits, budget committee will greenlight the ARR." — VP Product

Risks / sensitivities:
- High regulatory scrutiny (GLBA/PCI overlap) — any private deployment must support on-prem option for last-mile redaction.
- Cost sensitivity around burst pricing; pushing Redwood for a predictable burst rate cap.

Stubs/links: pricing deck, security FAQ (drive links above), load test report attached to ticket RED-1432.
